devdoc.details: This is an implementation of an on-chain multi-sign. On-chain multi-sign ensures that a quorum of signatures needs to be submitted before the transaction is passed on to the ERC20 contract(in our case). To verify signatures and hash data in a particular way, we use the EIP712.sol scheme: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/EIPS/eip-712.md.

ECDSAInvalidSignatureLength(uint256).details: The signature has an invalid length.

ECDSAInvalidSignatureS(bytes32).details: The signature has an S value that is in the upper half order.

DestinationCalled(address,bytes,uint256).details: Event emitted when the destination contract is called with the provided calldata.

params.data: The encoded bytes that will lead to execution of a method and change state of the destination                    contract.
params.destination: The contract being called with the provided calldata.
params.gasLimit: The maximum amount of gas that can be consumed by the destination contract to execute the                    calldata.

SignersChanged(address,address[],uint8[].details: Event emitted when the state of the contract changes.

params.account: The contract for which the signer information was updated, which is this.
params.quorum: The cumulative weight of all signatures should exceed or match this value.
params.signers: The new array of signer address.
params.weights: The new array of weights of the signers.

execute(uint8[],bytes32[],bytes32[],addr.details: This method is called by an EOA/funding account with the correct set of signatures to eventually make a call to the `destination` with provided call data. Example, calls to the ERC20 contract are made from this method for all MultiSign accounts.

setSigners(address[],uint8[],uint256).details: This method facilitates changing the signer addresses, their weights and quorum. Since this method changes the state of the contract, it emits the `SignersChanged` event at the end of successful execution. This method can be called by this contract only in order to verify that the signatures are from existing signers with privilege to do so.

signerWeight(address).details: Given an address of a signer, return the weight of it's signature that gets counted for this account.

signers().details: Returns the list of signer addresses in an array.

constructor.notice: Default constructor to initialize the MultiSign contract. Signer addresses submitted to the contract should be ordered by their string values.*

nonce().notice: Every transaction submitted to this contract should have a nonce associated to it just like any other EOA or Contract Account. This state variable holds that value.

quorum().notice: A state variable to store the total weight of all signatures required to successfully finish execution of the `execute` method.
